title: Read the annual-energy number
hook: Two illustrative annual labels differ. How does that difference repeat over years?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Translate a stated annual energy figure into a multiyear running-cost model.

misconception: An annual energy label is already the multiyear cost.
objective: Translate a stated annual energy figure into a multiyear running-cost model.

claims.text: Illustrative annual quantities are 200kWh and 350kWh. Both are priced at €0.30/kWh every year. Scaled model; illustrative:200-or-350kWh/year;€0.30/kWh;constant years.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Years=2, A=€120 and B=€210. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",200,"x",0.3]; B=["*",350,"x",0.3]; x denotes Years. At x=2, A=120, B=210. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Multiply annual energy by years and the stated unit price. This extrapolation assumes unchanged use and tariff; it is not a measured forecast for a named product.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",200,"x",0.3]; B=["*",350,"x",0.3]; x denotes Years. At x=2, A=120, B=210. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: An illustrative label states 250kWh per year. At an unchanged fictional €0.30/kWh, what is the modeled running cost over four years? Correct: €300. Annual energy × years × price: 250 × 4 × €0.30 = €300. The label is one year, not the multiyear cost.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. recall.question: An illustrative label states 250kWh per year. At an unchanged fictional €0.30/kWh, what is the modeled running cost over four years?
recall.why: Annual energy × years × price: 250 × 4 × €0.30 = €300. The label is one year, not the multiyear cost.
